title: The Kinzie house of 1812 rebuilt to Juliette Kinzie's own sketch
items: The Kinzie house's main roof now runs down over the piazza and breaks to a flatter pitch, and the piazza's posts stand nearly as tall as the walls. That is how Sarony's lithograph of Juliette Kinzie's sketch draws it. She was the one artist who lived beside the house. The other old pictures agree once the roof is built that way.

The west end now has a small window high in the gable, a second window and a side door. The east end has two small windows under the eaves, as the earliest picture of the house, from 1820, shows them.
Sarony's lithograph joins the six other pictures the house is compared against.
